programme_info.title: B.Tech. in Electrical and Electronics Engineering

programme_educational_objectives.description: To prepare under graduate students to excel in technical profession/industry and/or higher education by providing a strong foundation in mathematics, science and engineering.

To transform engineering students to expert engineers so that they could comprehend, analyse, design and create novel products and solutions to Electrical and Electronics Engineering problems that are technically sound, economically feasible and socially acceptable.
To train students to exhibit professionalism, keep up ethics in their profession and relate engineering issues to address the technical and social challenges.
To develop communication skills and team work and to nurture multidisciplinary approach in problem solving.

programme_outcomes.title: Engineering knowledge
programme_outcomes.description: Apply the knowledge of mathematics, science, engineering fundamentals, and an engineering specialization to the solution of complex engineering problems.

programme_outcomes.title: Problem analysis
programme_outcomes.description: Identify, formulate, research literature, and analyse complex engineering problems reaching substantiated conclusions using first principles of mathematics, natural sciences, and engineering sciences.

programme_outcomes.title: Design/development of solutions
programme_outcomes.description: Design solutions for complex engineering problems and design system components or processes that meet the specified needs with appropriate consideration for the public health and safety, and the cultural, societal, and environmental considerations.

programme_outcomes.title: Conduct investigations of complex problems
programme_outcomes.description: Use research-based knowledge and research methods including design of experiments, analysis and interpretation of data, and synthesis of the information to provide valid conclusions.

programme_outcomes.title: Modern tool usage
programme_outcomes.description: Create, select, and apply appropriate techniques, resources, and modern engineering and IT tools including prediction and modelling to complex engineering activities with an understanding of the limitations.

programme_outcomes.title: The engineer and society
programme_outcomes.description: Apply reasoning informed by the contextual knowledge to assess societal, health, safety, legal and cultural issues and the consequent responsibilities relevant to the professional engineering practice.

programme_outcomes.title: Environment and sustainability
programme_outcomes.description: Understand the impact of the professional engineering solutions in societal and environmental contexts, and demonstrate the knowledge of, and need for sustainable development.

programme_outcomes.title: Ethics
programme_outcomes.description: Apply ethical principles and commit to professional ethics and responsibilities and norms of the engineering practice.

programme_outcomes.title: Individual and team work
programme_outcomes.description: Function effectively as an individual, and as a member or leader in diverse teams, and in multidisciplinary settings.

programme_outcomes.title: Communication
programme_outcomes.description: Communicate effectively on complex engineering activities with the engineering community and with society at large, such as, being able to comprehend and write effective reports and design documentation, make effective presentations, and give and receive clear instructions.

programme_outcomes.title: Project management and finance
programme_outcomes.description: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of the engineering and management principles and apply these to one's own work, as a member and leader in a team, to manage projects and in multidisciplinary environments.

programme_outcomes.title: Life-long learning
programme_outcomes.description: Recognize the need for, and have the preparation and ability to engage in independent and life-long learning in the broadest context of technological change.

programme_specific_outcomes.description: Identify, formulate and analyse real-life electrical and electronics engineering problems by way of utilising the knowledge of mathematics, science and engineering principles.

Design and develop sophisticated equipment and experimental systems for carrying out detailed investigation to multifaceted electrical and electronics engineering problems leading to reliable and feasible solutions for the same utilising all the available tools.

Work as an electrical or electronics engineer who is capable of identifying solutions to various local and global problems faced by the society, up keeping a pollution free environment without compromising professional ethics and social values.

Think independently, take initiative, lead a team of engineers or researchers, communicate orally as well as in writing with others, participate in various professional activities, take up administrative responsibilities and thus maintain lifelong learning process.

categories.name: Activity Credits
categories.notes: Minimum 80 Activity Points required. Min 20 points by end of S4, min 40 by end of S6.

effort_notation.P: Practical — one unit is one-hour duration
effort_notation.O: Outside the class effort / self-study — one unit is one-hour duration

semester_plan.notes: Students choose ONE of three options for slots 1 (and optionally 2) below:

core_courses.title: Mathematics I
course_outcomes: CO1: Formulate some engineering problems as ODEs and hence solve such problems.
CO2: Solve linear ODEs with constant coefficients.
CO3: Find the limits, check for continuity and differentiability of real valued functions of two variables.
CO4: Test for the convergence of sequences and series.
CO5: Find the Fourier series representing periodic functions.
topics: Existence and uniqueness of solution of first order ODE, methods of solutions, linear ODE, orthogonal trajectories
Linear homogeneous second order ODEs with constant coefficients, Wronskian, method of undetermined coefficients, variation of parameters, Euler-Cauchy equations, applications, system of linear ODEs

Functions of several variables: limit, continuity, partial derivatives, directional derivatives, gradient, local maxima/minima, saddle point, Taylor's formula, Hessian, second derivative test, Lagrange multipliers
Parameterised curves in space, arc length, tangent and normal vectors, curvature and torsion
Sequences, Cauchy sequence, convergence, series, tests for convergence, absolute convergence, power series, radius of convergence, Taylor series, Fourier series, Fourier integral, Fourier transforms
references: Anton, Bivens & Davis, Calculus, 10th ed., Wiley, 2015
Thomas, Weir & Hass, Thomas' Calculus, 12th ed., Pearson, 2015
Kreyszig, Advanced Engineering Mathematics, 10th ed., Wiley, 2015
Apostol, Calculus Vol 1, 1st ed., Wiley, 2014

core_courses.title: Mathematics II
course_outcomes: CO1: Find the parametric representation of curves and surfaces in space and evaluate integrals over curves and surfaces.
CO2: Use Laplace transform and its properties to solve differential equations and integral equations.
CO3: Test the consistency of the system of linear equations and solve it.
CO4: Diagonalise symmetric matrices and use it to find the nature of quadratic forms.
topics: Vector field, divergence, curl, scalar potential, line integral, double/triple integrals, Green's theorem, Gauss' divergence theorem, Stokes' theorem
Laplace transform, inverse Laplace transform, Dirac delta function, convolution, solution of ODEs and integral equations
System of linear equations, Gauss elimination, LU decomposition, rank, eigenvalues, eigenvectors, Cayley-Hamilton theorem, diagonalisation, quadratic forms
references: Kreyszig, Advanced Engineering Mathematics, 10th ed., Wiley, 2015
Anton, Bivens & Davis, Calculus, 10th ed., Wiley, 2015
Arnold, Ordinary Differential Equations, Springer, 2006
Dyke, An Introduction to Laplace Transforms and Fourier Series, Springer, 2014

core_courses.title: Mathematics III
topics: Complex analysis
Numerical methods
Special functions (as per Math III syllabus)
core_courses.notes: Detailed syllabus not extracted from available pages — refer to department for full content.

core_courses.title: Mathematics IV
course_outcomes: CO1: Model managerial problems in industries to linear programming problems and solve using various techniques and algorithms.
CO2: Model and solve PDEs using analytic methods.
CO3: Apply the basics of probability theory in solving real life problems.
CO4: Identify the distribution and transform random variables.
topics: Linear Programming: formulation, graphical method, simplex method, duality theory, dual simplex method, primal-dual algorithm
PDEs: Cauchy's problem, quasilinear and nonlinear PDEs, wave equation, heat equation, Laplace equation, Fourier series, Laplace transforms
Probability distributions: random variables, expectation, variance, binomial, Poisson, geometric, normal, uniform, gamma, beta, Weibull distributions
Transformation of random variables, jointly distributed random variables, correlation, bivariate normal distribution
references: Mohan & Deep, Optimization Techniques, New Age International, 2009
Wayne Winston, Operations Research, Cengage Learning, 4th ed., 2011
Greenspan, Introduction to Partial Differential Equations, Dover, 2000
Kreyszig, Advanced Engineering Mathematics, Wiley, 9th ed., 2012
Ross, A First Course in Probability, 9th ed., Pearson, 2014

core_courses.title: Engineering Graphics
course_outcomes: CO1: Make use of the Indian Standard Code of Practice in Engineering Drawing.
CO2: Represent any engineering object by its orthographic views.
CO3: Convert orthographic views of an engineering object into its isometric view.
CO4: Use software for drawing and visualization of engineering objects.
topics: Drawing instruments, lines, lettering, dimensioning, AutoCAD introduction, geometric construction, plain and diagonal scales
Orthographic projection (1st and 3rd angle) of points, lines, planes and solids in simple and oblique positions
Sections of solids, development of surfaces, isometric projection, introduction to perspective projection
references: Agrawal B. & Agrawal C.M., Engineering Drawing, 3rd ed., McGraw Hill, 2019
Bhatt N.D., Engineering Drawing, 54th ed., Charotar, 2023
Venugopal K. & Raja V.P., Engineering Drawing + AutoCAD, 6th ed., New Age, 2022

core_courses.title: Electricity and Magnetism
course_outcomes: CO1: Apply knowledge of vector calculus to describe Electric and Magnetic fields.
CO2: Identify simplifying principles like symmetry to compute Electric and Magnetic fields.
CO3: Formulate and solve problems involving time dependent electromagnetic fields using Maxwell's equations.
CO4: Analyse propagation of electromagnetic waves in vacuum and dielectric media.
topics: Electrostatics: Coulomb's law, Gauss law, potential, Poisson and Laplace equations, dielectrics
Magnetostatics: Biot-Savart law, Ampere's law, magnetostatic energy, magnetized materials
Time varying fields: Faraday's law, Maxwell's equations, displacement current, Poynting's theorem
Electromagnetic waves: wave equation, plane wave solution, propagation in dielectric media
references: Griffiths, Introduction to Electrodynamics, 4th ed., PHI, 2015
Purcell & Morin, Electricity and Magnetism, 3rd ed., Cambridge, 2013
Sadiku & Kulkarni, Principles of Electromagnetics, 6th ed., Oxford, 2015
Cheng, Field and Wave Electromagnetics, 2nd ed., Pearson, 2014

core_courses.title: Professional Communication
course_outcomes: CO1: Distinguish the role and purpose of communication at the workplace and for academic purposes.
CO2: Decide strategies and modes for effective communication in a dynamic workplace.
CO3: Combine multiple approaches for successful and ethical information exchange.
CO4: Estimate best communication practices to assist productivity and congeniality at the workplace.
topics: Listening and reading comprehension: conversation skills, describing graphs/tables, listening for specific purposes
Vocabulary and speaking: professional vocabulary, reading strategies, critical reading, text structures
Effective writing: note making, paragraph writing, official letters, emails, abstract writing
Communication at workplace: communication theory, verbal/nonverbal, group discussions, presentations, digital communication, ethical communication
references: Bhatnagar N & Bhatnagar M, Communicative English for Engineers and Professionals, Dorling Kindersley, 2010
Garner B.A., HBR Guide to Better Business Writing, Harvard Business Review Press, 2012
Hewings M., Advanced Grammar in Use, Cambridge University Press, 2013

core_courses.title: Professional Ethics
course_outcomes: CO1: Develop a clear understanding of human values and use it as basis for all activities.
CO2: Understand and follow the ethical aspects of engineering profession.
CO3: Align with the Code of Ethics prescribed by IEEE in all professional activities.
CO4: Assimilate the elements of academic integrity and Honour Codes.
topics: Human values: morals, integrity, work ethic, civic virtue, honesty, empathy, self-confidence, character
Ethics in professional practice: ethical responsibilities to consumers, safety, intellectual property, environment and sustainability
IEEE code of ethics, academic integrity: plagiarism, Honour Codes
references: Naagarazan R.S., A Textbook on Professional Ethics and Human Values, 3rd ed., New Age International, 2022
Bainbridge A.F., Ethics for Engineers: A Brief Introduction, CRC Press, 2021
IEEE Code of Ethics — https://www.ieee.org/about/corporate/governance/p7-8.html

core_courses.title: Introduction to Electrical Engineering
course_outcomes: CO1: Explain characteristics of voltage sources, current sources and passive circuit elements.
CO2: Solve simple magnetic and capacitive circuits for signal and power processing.
CO3: Analyse electrical circuits using various circuit analysis methods and circuit theorems.
CO4: Analyse single phase ac circuits.
CO5: Analyse balanced and unbalanced three-phase ac circuits.
topics: Resistive circuits: v-i relationships, Kirchhoff's laws, Node voltage and Mesh current analysis, dependent sources, source transformation, Star-Delta conversion
Circuit theorems: Superposition, Thevenin, Norton, Maximum Power Transfer, Reciprocity; magnetic circuits, inductance, capacitance
Single-phase AC circuits: phasor representation, impedance/admittance, resonance, power factor, complex power
Three-phase AC circuits: balanced/unbalanced systems, symmetrical components, sequence decoupling
references: Suresh Kumar K.S., Electric Circuits & Networks, Pearson, 2009
Nilsson & Riedel, Electric Circuits, 8th ed., Pearson, 2002
Desoer & Kuh, Basic Circuit Theory, McGraw Hill, 2009
Edminister, Electric Circuit Theory, Schaum's, 6th ed., McGraw Hill, 2014

core_courses.title: Electrical Measurements
course_outcomes: CO1: Familiarization with different types of electrical measurement systems.
CO2: Analyze working principles of resistance, inductance, capacitance and magnetic quantity measurements.
CO3: Analyze working principles of waveform measurements.
CO4: Perform measurement of power & energy in poly phase systems.
topics: Voltage and current measurements: instruments, errors, moving coil/iron instruments, instrument transformers, digital instruments
Magnetic measurements: ballistic galvanometer, BH curve and Hysteresis loop
Waveform measurements: CRO, DSO, Lissajous patterns
Bridge measurements: Wheatstone, Kelvin, Maxwell, Hay's, Schering, Wien bridges
Power and energy measurements: dynamometer wattmeters, three-phase power, energy meters, kVA measurement
references: Golding E.W., Electrical Measurements & Measuring Instruments, 6th ed., Reem, 2019
Sawhney A.K., Electrical and Electronic Measurements and Instrumentation, Dhanpat Rai, 2015

core_courses.title: Electronic Circuits - I
course_outcomes: CO1: Design rectifiers, clipping circuits, DC restoration circuits and voltage regulators using diodes and zener diodes.
CO2: Design biasing circuits for BJTs, JFETs and MOSFETs.
CO3: Design single-stage and multi-stage amplification systems.
CO4: Design Class A, Class B and Class AB power stages using BJTs.
CO5: Conduct performance evaluation of prototype amplifier designs by small signal analysis.
CO6: Choose digital components from various logic families.
topics: Semiconductor devices: diodes, BJT, JFET, MOSFET — capacitances, biasing, small signal models
Diode circuits: rectifiers, filters, clipping, clamping, zener regulators
Amplifier midband analysis: CE, CB, emitter follower, common source, common drain amplifiers; Class A, B, AB power amplifiers
Digital logic families: DTL, TTL, Schottky TTL, ECL, CMOS — propagation delays, speed-power product
references: Sedra & Smith, Microelectronic Circuits, 5th ed., Oxford, 2009
Millman J., Microelectronics, 2nd ed., McGraw-Hill, 2005
Boylestad & Nashelsky, Electronic Devices and Circuit Theory, 10th ed., Pearson, 2009

core_courses.title: Circuits and Networks
course_outcomes: CO1: Analyse dynamic and steady state response of electrical circuits in time domain.
CO2: Analyse dynamic and steady state response in frequency domain.
CO3: Examine first-order and second-order circuits for signal processing tasks.
CO4: Solve two-port systems by applying two-port network modelling.
topics: Time-domain analysis: RL, RC, RLC circuits; initial conditions; step, ramp, impulse responses
Frequency-domain analysis: Laplace transforms, s-domain circuit analysis, transfer functions, poles and zeros
Sinusoidal steady-state, Fourier series, THD, non-sinusoidal periodic inputs
Two-port networks: Z, Y, h, ABCD parameters; interconnections; feedback systems
references: Suresh Kumar K.S., Electric Circuits and Networks, Pearson, 2009
Van Valkenburg M.E., Network Analysis, 3rd ed., Pearson, 2019
Hayt & Kemmerly, Engineering Circuit Analysis, 9th ed., McGraw-Hill, 2020

core_courses.title: Engineering Mechanics
course_outcomes: CO1: Determine the resultants of a force system.
CO2: Solve rigid body statics problems using equations of equilibrium.
CO3: Determine the first and second moments of area for planar surfaces.
CO4: Perform kinematic analysis of particles.
CO5: Solve particle dynamics problems using Newton's laws, energy methods and momentum methods.
topics: Equivalent force systems, vector algebra, resultant of force systems
Rigid body statics: equilibrium, friction, static indeterminacy
Properties of surfaces: centroid, moments of area
Particle kinematics: velocity and acceleration in various coordinate systems
Particle dynamics: Newton's laws, energy methods, momentum methods
references: Shames & Rao, Engineering Mechanics, 4th ed., Pearson, 2005
Beer, Johnston et al., Vector Mechanics for Engineers, 12th ed., McGraw Hill, 2019
Hibbeler, Engineering Mechanics, 14th ed., Pearson, 2017

core_courses.title: Digital Circuits and Systems
course_outcomes: CO1: Formulate Combinational Logic Problems and perform Logic Optimization.
CO2: Design combinational logic using standard SSI/MSI gates, MUX, ROM, PLA, PAL.
CO3: Perform design verification/validation of synchronous and asynchronous sequential circuits.
CO4: Design synchronous and asynchronous sequential circuits.
topics: Boolean functions, Karnaugh maps, NAND/NOR/EX-OR implementation
Binary number representations, MSI/LSI combinational circuits: adders, comparators, MUX, decoders
Sequential circuits: latches, flip-flops, shift registers, counters
FSM analysis and design: state reduction, synchronous and asynchronous sequential logic, hazards
Memory: RAM, ROM, PROM, PLA, PAL, FPGAs, VHDL introduction
references: Mano & Ciletti, Digital Design, 6th ed., Pearson, 2018
Roth, Fundamentals of Logic Design, 7th ed., Jaico, 2013
Floyd, Digital Fundamentals, 11th ed., Prentice Hall, 2017

core_courses.title: Signals and Systems
course_outcomes: CO1: Design and validate simple first and second order linear continuous-time systems.
CO2: Evaluate multi-order LTI System designs by Impulse Response Test.
CO3: Evaluate stability and stability margins by transfer function approach.
CO4: Design first/second order systems for basic signal/energy processing applications.
CO5: Evaluate signal distortion characteristics of a transmission channel.
topics: First-order CT-LTI systems: signal classification, system elements, differential equations, time constants, first-order dynamics
Higher-order systems: second-order systems, convolution, impulse response, stability
Frequency-domain: Fourier transforms, linear distortion, sampling theorem, Nyquist's theorem
Laplace transforms: ROC, transfer functions, poles and zeros
references: Lathi B.P., Signal Processing and Linear Systems, 2nd ed., Oxford, 2006
Oppenheim & Schafer, Discrete-Time Signal Processing, 3rd ed., Pearson, 2014
Haykin & Van Veen, Signals and Systems, 2nd ed., Wiley, 2009

core_courses.title: Microprocessors and Microcontrollers
course_outcomes: CO1: Explain the basics of Digital Systems.
CO2: Discuss the working of a microprocessor/controller.
CO3: Develop and test programs using assembly/high-level language.
CO4: Test the working of different peripherals in a digital system.
CO5: Design, modify, compile and debug assembly/C programs for PIC microcontroller.
topics: Number systems, computer architecture, CISC vs RISC, Von-Neumann vs Harvard architecture
PIC 18F452 Microcontroller: architecture, assembly language, MPLAB IDE, I/O ports, timers, interrupts, C programming
Intel 8086: architecture, addressing modes, instruction set, assembly programming, interrupts, interfacing ICs (8255, 8253, 8251, 8257, 8259)
references: Muhammad Ali Mazidi et al., PIC Microcontroller and Embedded Systems, Pearson, 2021
Lyla B Das, The x86 Microprocessors, Pearson India, 2014

core_courses.title: Electrical Machines - I
course_outcomes: CO1: Discuss fundamental principles and classification of electromagnetic machines.
CO2: Analyse constructional details and principle of operation of DC machines.
CO3: Evaluate operation, testing and applications of DC generators and motors.
CO4: Discuss constructional details and principle of operation of transformers.
CO5: Apply knowledge about testing and applications of transformers.
topics: Electromagnetic machines: principles, armature windings, MMF, torque, EMF equations
DC machines: construction, magnetic circuit, emf equation, armature reaction, commutation
DC generators and motors: circuit models, magnetisation characteristics, starting, speed control, testing (Swinburne, Hopkinson, Retardation)
Transformers: construction, equivalent circuit, efficiency, regulation, OC/SC tests, Sumpner's test, three-phase connections, auto-transformers
references: Clayton & Hancock, Performance and Design of DC Machines, ELBS, 1971
Nagarath & Kothari, Electric Machines, Tata McGraw Hill, 1999
Say M.G., Performance and Design of AC Machines, CBS, 1983

core_courses.title: Electronic Circuits – II
course_outcomes: CO1: Design discrete transistor amplification circuits with given gain and bandwidth.
CO2: Design linear signal processing application circuits using Opamps.
CO3: Apply voltage regulator ICs for power supply design.
CO4: Carry out stability analysis on amplifying circuits and design compensators.
CO5: Design sinusoidal oscillators using Opamps.
CO6: Design transistorized Bistable, Astable and Monostable circuits.
topics: Frequency response of discrete amplifiers (s-domain): low and high frequency response of BJT/FET amplifiers, Miller effect
Basic Opamp circuits: differential amplifiers, CMRR, ideal/practical Opamps, linear applications (integrator, differentiator, instrumentation amplifier)
Non-linear Opamp applications: comparators, Schmitt trigger, astable multivibrator, square-triangle generator
Feedback amplifiers and stability: Barkhausen criterion, gain/phase margin, compensation, sinusoidal oscillators, crystal oscillators
Bistable and metastable transistor circuits
references: Sedra & Smith, Microelectronic Circuits, 5th ed., Oxford, 2009
Sergio Franco, Design with Op-Amps and Analog ICs, Tata McGraw-Hill, 2005

core_courses.title: Power Systems - I
course_outcomes: CO1: Analyse and compare the economics of various electrical energy sources.
CO2: Analyse the performance of transmission lines.
CO3: Design electrical and mechanical parameters of power system.
CO4: Model power systems using single line diagrams and analyse using load flow methods.
CO5: Evaluate and analyse various distribution schemes.
topics: Power generation and economics: conventional/renewable sources, load factor, tariffs
Transmission line parameters: resistance, inductance, capacitance, GMD/GMR, ABCD constants, Ferranti effect, corona, mechanical design
Underground cables: types, insulation resistance, capacitance
Load flow studies: bus matrices, Gauss-Seidel, Newton-Raphson, Fast decoupled, DC load flow
Distribution systems: Kelvin's law, voltage control, microgrids, smart grids
references: Grainger & Stevenson, Power System Analysis, McGraw-Hill, 2017
Kothari, Nagrath & Saket, Modern Power System Analysis, 5th ed., 2022
Saadat, Power System Analysis, 4th ed., Tata McGraw Hill, 2011

core_courses.title: Power Electronics
course_outcomes: CO1: Understand characteristics of important power semiconductor switches.
CO2: Analyze power electronic switch-based rectifiers, converters and inverters.
CO3: Select circuit elements required for a Power Electronic system.
CO4: Design a power electronic system for a given application.
topics: Power semiconductor switches: diodes, thyristors, IGBTs, MOSFETs, gate driver circuits, snubber circuits
Controlled rectifiers: single-phase and three-phase phase-controlled rectifiers
Inverters: single-phase half/full-bridge, three-phase, SPWM, bipolar/unipolar PWM, grid-tied inverters
DC-DC converters: Buck, Boost, Buck-Boost; design of inductors, transformers, heat sinks
references: Umanand L., Power Electronics: Essentials and Applications, Wiley India, 2009
Ned Mohan, Power Electronics, Wiley, 2nd ed., 1995
Rashid, Power Electronics, Pearson, 3rd ed., 2004

core_courses.title: Electrical Machines - II
course_outcomes: CO1: Know constructional details and principle of operation of alternators.
CO2: Know working of synchronous machines as generators and motors.
CO3: Know constructional details and principle of operation of induction motors.
CO4: Know speed control, testing and applications of induction motors.
CO5: Know generalized machine theory and simulation methods.
topics: Alternators: construction, armature reaction, voltage regulation (EMF, MMF, Potier methods), two-reaction theory, excitation
Synchronous machines: power angle characteristics, load sharing, V curves, hunting, starting methods
Induction machines: equivalent circuit, torque-slip characteristics, starting, speed control, induction generators
Generalized machine theory: machine as a circuit, digital simulation
references: Nagarath & Kothari, Electric Machines, Tata McGraw Hill, 1999
Say M.G., Performance and Design of AC Machines, CBS, 1983
Chapman S.J., Electric Machine Fundamentals, McGraw Hill, 1999

core_courses.title: Control Systems - I
course_outcomes: CO1: Represent dynamical systems using transfer function models.
CO2: Analyze system response and stability using time-domain methods.
CO3: Analyze system response and stability using frequency-domain methods.
CO4: Design compensators using time and frequency domain techniques.
CO5: Analyze system response and design compensators using simulation tools.
topics: Modelling: differential equations, transfer functions, block diagrams, signal flow graphs, Mason's gain formula
Time-domain analysis: transient response, steady-state error, Routh-Hurwitz criterion, root locus
Frequency-domain analysis: Bode, Nyquist, Polar plots, gain margin, phase margin
Controllers: P, PI, PD, PID — tuning methods; Lead, Lag, Lead-Lag compensators
references: Ogata K., Modern Control Engineering, 5th ed., Pearson, 2015
Nagrath & Gopal, Control Systems Engineering, 7th ed., Tata McGraw Hill, 2021
Nise N.S., Control Systems Engineering, Wiley, 7th ed., 2014

core_courses.title: Digital Signal Processing
course_outcomes: CO1: Analyze discrete time systems using time domain and frequency domain methods.
CO2: Design and validate linear phase FIR systems.
CO3: Design IIR and FIR filter structures for filtering applications.
CO4: Analyze spectrum of periodic CT waveforms using Digital Spectrum Analyzer.
CO5: Design Digital Filters by Block Convolution.
topics: DT signals and LTI-DT systems: ZIR, ZSR, natural frequencies, stability, frequency response
Z-transforms: properties, transfer functions, poles/zeros, linear phase FIR types
IIR/FIR filter design: Butterworth approximation, bilinear transformation, windowing, filter structures
DFT, FFT: Radix-2 DIT/DIF FFT, block convolution, spectral analysis
references: Proakis & Manolakis, Digital Signal Processing, 4th ed., Pearson, 2013
Oppenheim & Schafer, Discrete-Time Signal Processing, 3rd ed., Pearson, 2014
Mitra, Digital Signal Processing: A Computer-Based Approach, 4th ed., McGraw-Hill, 2013

core_courses.title: Power Systems - II
course_outcomes: CO1: Examine and analyse the behaviour of faulted power systems.
CO2: Design protection schemes for power systems.
CO3: Select appropriate relay settings for overcurrent and distance relays.
CO4: Interpret generation control and economic dispatch methods.
CO5: Determine and analyse stability issues.
CO6: Analyse quenching mechanisms in circuit breakers.
topics: Fault analysis: symmetrical and unsymmetrical faults (LG, LL, LLG), impedance matrix methods, symmetrical components
Economic dispatch: B-coefficient, optimal load flow, AGC, automatic voltage regulation, SCADA
Power system stability: steady-state and transient stability, swing equation, equal area criterion
Switchgear and protection: overcurrent, distance, differential relays; digital and numerical relays; circuit breakers
references: Horowitz, Phadke & Henville, Power System Relaying, 5th ed., Wiley, 2022
Stevenson, Elements of Power System Analysis, McGraw Hill, 4th ed., 2015
Kothari & Nagrath, Power System Engineering, 3rd ed., Tata McGraw-Hill, 2019

core_courses.title: Control Systems - II
course_outcomes: CO1: Develop state space models for continuous-time systems and analyze their time response.
CO2: Design controllers and observers for dynamical systems using state feedback.
CO3: Model, analyse and design controllers for discrete time dynamical systems.
CO4: Analyse characteristics and assess stability of nonlinear dynamical systems.
CO5: Evaluate dynamical systems performance using simulation tools.
topics: State space analysis: canonical forms, eigenvalues, solution of state equations, state transition matrix
State-feedback design: controllability, observability, pole placement, Ackermann's formula, observers
Digital control systems: pulse transfer function, Z-domain stability, Jury's test
Nonlinear systems: phase plane analysis, limit cycles, Lyapunov's methods, describing functions
references: Ogata K., Modern Control Engineering, 5th ed., Pearson, 2015
Gopal M., Digital Control and State Variable Methods, 4th ed., Tata McGraw Hill, 2017
Khalil H.K., Nonlinear Systems, 3rd ed., Prentice Hall, 2002

core_courses.title: Analog Integrated Circuits
course_outcomes: CO1: Select the right Opamp for linear and non-linear applications.
CO2: Develop insight into working of BJT and MOSFET based Opamps.
CO3: Design simple waveform generation circuits.
CO4: Apply PLL, Multiplier ICs, RMS-DC converters to build signal processing subsystems.
CO5: Design custom-made single Opamp biquad cascade filters.
CO6: Apply S/H amplifiers and data converters for signal conversion systems.
topics: Review of linear Opamp applications, effect of finite GBP, integrators, differentiators, instrumentation amplifiers
Internal analysis of 741 IC, two-stage CMOS Opamp, folded cascode CMOS Opamp
Comparators, astable multivibrators, VCOs, function generators, PLL (NE564, CD4046)
Signal conditioning: Butterworth/Sallen-Key/KHN filters, active filter design
Signal conversion: ADC and DAC (SAR, successive approximation, R/2R ladder), sample-and-hold
references: Sedra & Smith, Microelectronic Circuits, 3rd ed., Holt Saunders, 1989
Franco, Design with Op-Amps and Analog ICs, McGraw Hill, 1988
Van Valkenburg, Analog Filter Design, Oxford, 2001

core_courses.title: Introduction to Communication Systems
course_outcomes: CO1: Understand mathematical concepts on signals and random processes for communication system design.
CO2: Acquire knowledge on various Amplitude Modulation Techniques.
CO3: Acquire knowledge on various Angle Modulation Techniques.
CO4: Acquire knowledge on PAM and PCM systems.
CO5: Become familiar with various line codes for Digital Base Band Transmission.
CO6: Become familiar with various Keying Schemes for Digital Carrier-Based Transmission.
topics: Mathematical preliminaries: correlation, signal space, random processes, noise in communication channels
Continuous-wave modulation: AM, DSBSC, SSB, FM, PM
Pulse code modulation: PAM, quantization, PCM, Delta Modulation, TDM
Digital communications: line codes, matched filtering, BPSK, QPSK, DPSK, FSK, error probability calculations
references: Taub & Schilling, Principles of Communication Systems, 2nd ed., McGraw-Hill
Haykin S., Communication Systems, 4th ed., Wiley, 2004
Dennis Roddy & John Coolen, Electronic Communication, 4th ed., Pearson, 2004

core_courses.title: Instrumentation Systems
course_outcomes: CO1: Describe working of active and passive sensors/transducers for nonelectrical quantities.
CO2: Select sensors for measurement of nonelectrical quantities in process industries.
CO3: Devise an appropriate signal conditioning circuit for a measurement system.
